claims.claim: Cache efficacy depends on placing static content before dynamic content in request order
claims.citation: Cache dziala prefiksowo - wszystko od poczatku requesta do breakpointu wlacznie jest kandydatem do cache hit, wszystko po breakpoincie jest platne per request (regular input tokens).

claims.claim: Anthropic API natural request order (tools -> system -> messages) already aligns with cache optimization hierarchy
claims.citation: Naturalny porzadek Anthropic API (tools -> system -> messages) juz sprzyja temu patternowi - tools zmieniaja sie najrzadziej, system rzadko, messages najczesciej.

claims.claim: Single breakpoint at end of static content is recommended default pattern for 80% of use cases
claims.citation: Wzorzec 1: Single breakpoint (80% use cases) - Rekomendowany jako default. Jeden cache_control na ostatnim blokku statycznym

claims.claim: Two-breakpoint strategy suits systems with mixed freshness requirements (rules vs daily data)
claims.citation: Dla systemow z mieszana zmianami: rules_and_rarely_changing_content z 1h TTL + today_rag_documents z default 5m TTL

claims.claim: Automatic top-level cache_control moves breakpoint forward each turn in multi-turn conversations
claims.citation: Automatic caching z top-level flagiem - System sam umiesci breakpoint na ostatnim cacheable bloku w messages, w kolejnym requestcie automatycznie przesunie breakpoint do przodu

claims.claim: Prefix promotion strategy amortizes cache write cost across many batch requests
claims.citation: Step 1: Wyslij jeden request z pelnym prefiksem, Step 2: Teraz WSZYSTKIE subsequent requests z tym samym prefix daja cache hit

claims.claim: Any change to tool definitions mid-session invalidates entire tools cache layer
claims.citation: Rejestruj wszystkie tools na starcie sesji... NIE edytuj tool description mid-session (nawet drobna zmiana = pelny rebuild)

claims.claim: Few-shot examples must be placed in system prompt, never in messages, for cache efficiency
claims.citation: DOBRZE: system z examples + cache_control,Messages z current_query. Cache cleanly hits na examples

claims.claim: Timestamps in system prompt destroy cache on every request because they change per call
claims.citation: Anti-pattern: f'You are a helpful assistant. Today is {datetime.now()}... Ten timestamp na poczatku DESTROYS cache przy kazdym requestcie'

claims.claim: User-specific data in system prompt creates unique cache entry per user instead of shared cache
claims.citation: ZLE: system=f'Assistant for user {user_id}. Preferences: {user_prefs}... Kazdy user tworzy unique cache entry'

claims.claim: Claude Code achieves 96% cache hit rate using <system-reminder> pattern for dynamic content in messages
claims.citation: Claude Code implementuje pattern <system-reminder>. Zamiast modyfikowac statyczny system prompt gdy kontekst sie zmienia, wstrzykuje dynamiczne dane jako tag w nastepnej wiadomosci uzytkownika. Cache hit rate: 96%
claims.source_location: section: Details / Claude Code architektura, paragraph 2-4

claims.claim: Kern-ai achieved 10x input cost reduction using 3-breakpoint strategy with snapped boundaries
claims.citation: Kern-ai osiagnela 10x redukcje input token cost. BP1 (~75k tokens, 1h TTL), BP2 (snap co 20 wiadomosci), BP3 (turn breakpoint). Mierzone wyniki: ~590k cached tokens z 600k total = 10x redukcja
claims.source_location: section: Details / Kern-ai case study, paragraph 1-3

claims.claim: Arxiv 2601.06007 empirical study shows 45-80% cost reduction is achievable across different strategies
claims.citation: Paper z arxiv.org (2601.06007): Cost reduction 45-80% w zaleznosci od strategii i providera, TTFT improvement 13-31% z optymalnych strategii

claims.claim: System-prompt-only caching consistently outperforms full-context caching for agentic tasks
claims.citation: System-prompt-only caching konsekwentnie LEPSZE niz full-context caching... Full-context (tool calls + results) moze degradowac latencje o 8.8%

claims.claim: Automatic cache lookback window checks only 20 blocks backward from breakpoint
claims.citation: Automatyczny lookback sprawdza tylko 20 blokow wstecz od breakpointu. Jesli konwersacja ma >20 blokow przed breakpointem, bloki wczesniejsze nie beda sprawdzane pod katem cache hit

claims.claim: Minimum token threshold for cache eligibility increased to 4096 for Opus 4.7, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5
claims.citation: Claude Opus 4.7: 4096, Claude Sonnet 4.6: 4096, Claude Haiku 4.5: 4096. Progi sa wyzsze niz wiele blogowych tutoriali zaklada
claims.source_location: section: Details / Aktualne minimalne progi tokenowe, table + paragraph 1

claims.claim: Cache write cost is 1.25x input token rate; break-even occurs after ~2-4 requests with same prefix
claims.citation: Cache bez reuse - single-shot request z cache_control placi 1.25x za nic... tylko gdy oczekujesz >=2 requestow z tym samym prefiksem

claims.claim: Dynamic tool generation via code interpreter preserves tools cache instead of invalidating it
claims.citation: Zamiast dodawac dynamiczne tools (ktore invaliduja cache), zaimplementuj generyczne 'code interpreter' tool i radzisz sobie z dynamika poprzez code generation. Cache narzedzia nigdy nie jest invalidowany

claims.claim: Snapped boundary strategy (multiple of 20) stabilizes breakpoint for 20 turns vs sliding window
claims.citation: Trick snapped boundaries: zamiast breakpoint = last_n_messages, uzyj breakpoint = (len(messages) // 20) * 20. Breakpoint stoi przez 20 tur - mniej invalidacji
claims.source_location: section: Details / Kern-ai case study, paragraph 3

claims.claim: Workspace-level isolation (since Feb 2026) means cache is shared within workspace but isolated between workspaces
claims.citation: Luty 2026 Anthropic wprowadzil workspace-level isolation... Cache jest shared wewnatrz workspace, ale nie miedzy workspaceami

claims.claim: Capitalization or whitespace drift in static content invalidates cache even if semantically identical
claims.citation: Capitalization drift - dwie literkowe zmiany kasuja cache. Zamiast tego: freeze text statycznych blokow, nie generuj ich dynamicznie

claims.claim: RAG systems should use dual breakpoint strategy: 1h TTL for rules, 5m TTL for document batches
claims.citation: Dwa breakpointy: Po system rules (1h TTL), Po RAG documents (5m TTL). 1h-cache entries musza appear BEFORE 5m-cache entries w requestcie

claims.claim: Agentic workflows benefit from automatic caching with frozen tools to preserve tool-layer cache
claims.citation: Dla multi-step agentow: tools: full set (static), system: role + workflow rules (static), messages: tool_use + tool_result history (growing, auto cache)... automatic caching jest kluczowy
claims.source_location: section: Details / Agentic workflow pattern, paragraph 1-2

claims.claim: Long conversations (>20 blocks) require additional breakpoints every ~15 blocks to avoid lookback misses
claims.citation: Rozwiazanie: Multi-breakpoint strategy dla dlugich konwersacji. Dodaj breakpoints co ~15-18 blokow (margin bezpieczenstwa przed limitem 20)

claims.claim: OpenAI automatic caching achieves 50% read cost savings; Anthropic explicit caching achieves 90% savings
claims.citation: OpenAI: Automatic caching dla promptow >1024 tokenow, Savings 50% na read. Anthropic: Explicite cache_control, Savings 90% na read

claims.claim: Tool array serialization order matters for cache; tools should be alphabetically ordered for consistency
claims.citation: Jezeli dzisiaj masz tools = [A, B, C] a jutro tools = [A, C, B], cache jest invalidated... Rekomendacja: alphabetyczny order tools (konsystentny serialization)
claims.source_location: section: Details / Tools best practice, paragraph 1-2

claims.claim: TTL values should default to 5 minutes for interactive chats and 1 hour for rarely-changing content
claims.citation: 9. 1h TTL dla krotkotrwalych konwersacji - placisz 2x write, nigdy nie dochodzisz do break-even. Zamiast tego: 5m default dla interaktywnych chatow

claims.claim: Maximum 4 explicit cache_control blocks recommended to avoid API errors
claims.citation: Maksimum 4 explicit breakpointy... bez sensu trzymac 1 jesli potrzeba 3
